clue.text: Ascetic knight in reasonable housing

indicators.note: housing means the word for reasonable holds the knight's letter inside it

parts.note: reasonable means fair
K is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A self-denying knight lodged in modest but decent quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A fakir is a Hindu or Muslim holy man who lives by begging and self-denial, an ascetic.

clue.text: Flippant and given to the party spirit — full of energy

indicators.note: full of means the word for partisan holds the energy letter within it

parts.note: factious means prone to faction, partisan
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A frivolous reveller, full of zest and enjoying the party atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party spirit' suggests festivity, but here it means partisan feeling, being factious.
explanation.definitionFit: Facetious remarks are joking at an inappropriate moment, so flippant.

clue.text: Child sent to head as criminal

parts.note: a kid is a child
napper is old British slang for the head

explanation.surface: A naughty child packed off to see the headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' suggests a headteacher; it is slang NAPPER. 'sent to' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A kidnapper is an offender who abducts people for ransom.

clue.text: Jotted down as one listened in mindless repetition

indicators.note: as one listened tells us to go by the sound of the word for jotted down

parts.note: jotted down means wrote

explanation.surface: Taking notes while hearing a lecture, without thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Rote is learning by mechanical memorisation without understanding.

clue.text: One doesn't have to work

parts.note: reads like someone idle or of independent means, but describes a person who offers labour freely, under no obligation

explanation.surface: Someone lucky enough not to need a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A volunteer works by choice, unpaid and not compelled.

clue.text: Us officer isn't perceived to be fashionable

indicators.note: read as able to be fashioned, so the letters of isn't perceived are shaped anew

explanation.surface: An American official who is not thought to be trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashionable' seems to mean stylish but is split as 'fashion-able', able to be reshaped.
explanation.definitionFit: The deputy to the head of state is a senior American office holder.

clue.text: Elegant cattle

definitions.meaning: ... in the sense of trim, tidy and stylish
an old word for cattle, oxen

explanation.definitionFit: Neat means smart and tidy, and is also an archaic term for bovine livestock.

clue.text: Period of raised expectation Conservative entered

indicators.note: entered means the Conservative letter goes inside the other word
raised means the word for expectation reads upwards in this down clue

parts.note: hope is expectation

explanation.surface: A time of heightened anticipation when the Tories came in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns HOPE into EPOH, and C goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is an era, a distinct stretch of time.

clue.text: Criminal charge I had — using speed

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in a murder rap
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A drug charge laid against someone found with amphetamine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speed' hints at the drug in the surface, but means quickness.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid describes moving fast, done with swiftness.

clue.text: Rebel's time as potential officer

parts.note: Jack Cade led the 1450 Kentish rebellion against Henry VI

explanation.surface: A rebel's spell in uniform as an officer in training.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade is a famous English rebel of the fifteenth century, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a trainee in the forces who may go on to become a commissioned officer.

clue.text: Prepare to fire a round, triumphant

parts.note: to cock a gun is to ready its hammer for firing
a hoop is a ring, something round

explanation.surface: Readying a gun for a shot, feeling pleased with oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Cock-a-hoop is an idiom for crowing with delight, exultant.

clue.text: Take great risk of judge's seriously adverse decision?

definitions.meaning: to invite ruin by reckless behaviour
read literally, a catastrophe handed down by a law court

explanation.surface: A gamble that ends in a crushing ruling from the bench.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to court ruin by recklessness, and read literally it is a catastrophe from a law court.

clue.text: Meal at motorway's side

parts.note: tea is a light evening meal in Britain
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: Eating a meal on the hard shoulder of a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' looks like part of the motorway picture but is the definition, a side being a team in sport.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport a side is the group of players representing one club or country.

clue.text: Jet failed when up

definitions.meaning: a jet of liquid, a stream gushing out
something 'up the' this word is ruined or has gone wrong, a British idiom

explanation.surface: An aircraft that broke down while airborne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up the spout' is British slang for ruined or failed, so the word that follows 'up' in that phrase is defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A spout is a gush of water or other liquid, and 'up the spout' idiomatically means wrecked.

clue.text: Woman had cast off

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
'd is the contracted form of had, as in I'd

explanation.surface: A woman who once had something has now got rid of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed something is to discard or throw it away, as a snake loses its skin.

clue.text: Eccentric sort of starting-handle

definitions.meaning: an odd person with strange obsessions
the bent handle once used to start a car engine by hand

explanation.definitionFit: A crank is both an oddball and an L-shaped lever for turning an engine over.

clue.text: Dotty piece of punctuation

parts.note: dotty suggests crazy, but here means made of dots, a mark of two stacked points

explanation.surface: A mad little punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: This mark consists of two dots, one above the other.

clue.text: He likes his work all right

definitions.text: He likes his work all right

parts.words: He likes his work all right
parts.note: sounds like a mildly contented worker, but means one who insists that every bit of his work be exactly right

explanation.surface: A man who is reasonably content with his job.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who demands flawlessness in everything wants work to be correct in all respects.

clue.text: Cheeky to accept volume, being bankrupt

indicators.note: to accept means the word for cheeky takes the volume letter inside

parts.note: insolent means cheeky, impertinent

explanation.surface: A rude debtor who takes a big book though broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unable to pay one's debts is the state of a ruined, bankrupt business.

clue.text: Shopkeeper barters on island

parts.note: to barter is to trade
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper swapping goods on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman is someone who sells goods in a shop or deals in a trade.

clue.text: Lucky to discover that sick poet is insured

indicators.note: sick means unwell or disordered, telling us the letters of poet is insured are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fortunate find: an ailing poet turns out to have insurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to discover that' is link text joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Serendipity is happy chance, making discoveries by accident, so fortunate.

clue.text: Money that's no more than one's due

definitions.text: Money that's no more than one's due

parts.words: Money that's no more than one's due
parts.note: suggests a fair payment one is owed, but means money owed by one, which is due to be paid

explanation.surface: A modest sum that is simply what one deserves.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum owed and payable to a creditor is an obligation that falls due.

clue.text: Cut up, having gambled

definitions.meaning: chopped into small cubes, in cooking

explanation.definitionFit: Diced means chopped into cubes, and also the past tense of to dice, to gamble.

clue.text: Sad music from royal horse guards?

definitions.meaning: a melancholy musical genre from the American South
the ... and Royals is a British household cavalry regiment, nicknamed this

explanation.surface: Mournful tunes played by a cavalry regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blues and Royals are a mounted regiment of the British Household Cavalry, formerly the Royal Horse Guards.
explanation.definitionFit: Blues is a melancholy music style, and the nickname of the Royal Horse Guards.

clue.text: Cycle, taking pulse after exercise

indicators.note: after places the word for pulse behind the abbreviation for exercise

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
dal is a dish of lentils or other pulses, as in Indian cooking

explanation.surface: A cyclist checks their heart rate after a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' tempts as a heartbeat, but here it is a pulse in the sense of lentils, DAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To cycle is to ride a bike, which one does by working its foot levers.

clue.text: Hear parasite run off

indicators.note: Hear tells us to take the word for parasite as it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a flea is a blood-sucking parasitic insect

explanation.surface: Listen to the bloodsucker scurrying away.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to escape or bolt, getting away quickly.

clue.text: Unoccupied, drop line in to fish

indicators.note: drop in means the line letter is put inside the word for fish

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, also called orfe

explanation.surface: With nothing to do, cast a line in for some fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means inactive, not busy with anything.

clue.text: Northerner putting son to bed?

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Someone putting their boy to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Scotland comes from Britain's north.

clue.text: The French revolution?

parts.note: points to the 1789 uprising, but means a revolution expressed in a French phrase, a sudden seizure of state power

explanation.surface: A history question about France's great upheaval.
explanation.definitionFit: This French term names a sudden overthrow of a government, a kind of revolution.

clue.text: A hundred sheets of paper, off-white

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a ream is a quantity of paper, nominally 500 sheets

explanation.surface: A stack of slightly yellowed paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream is a pale yellowish colour, just short of pure white.

clue.text: Dilapidated state is hell to put right

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, hell
to repair is to mend or fix

explanation.surface: A ruinous condition that is hellish to fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' and 'to' are link words; 'hell to put right' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Disrepair is the condition of something neglected and falling apart.

clue.text: Giant container army filled

indicators.note: filled means the soldiers' letters go into the container word

parts.note: a tin is a metal container
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: A huge vessel packed with troops.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were the giant elder gods of Greek myth, so anything colossal.
